extracted.intended_audience: general readers, television fans, media researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Encyclopedic documentation of a single television sitcom's broadcast history, ratings, critical reception, home media, and distribution. Focused on factual reporting of viewership, awards, scheduling, and related commercial/controversial events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total viewership (per-episode)
rubrics_metrics.description: The pilot episode generated 8.13 million viewers, the third-season premiere garnered 8.5 million viewers; season averages and lowest-rated episodes are reported (e.g., season average 6.23 million in original timeslot; lowest ratings for episodes that achieved 4.61 million viewers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a basic measure of a show's audience reach; the article lists per-episode and season-average viewer counts and highlights peaks and lows over the run.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adults 18–49 ratings / demographic ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Episode and premiere ratings in the adults 18–49 demographic are reported (example: third-season premiere earned a 4.1 preliminary adults 18–49 rating, a 21% increase from the second-season premiere). The show is also placed in demographic rankings (e.g., tied at number 85 in the 18–49 demographic during a period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertiser-coveted 18–49 demo figures are tracked separately from raw viewers and used to compare shows' advertising value.

rubrics_metrics.name: DVR/Time-shifted viewing impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Nielsen Media Research reported that 30 Rock adds nearly 7.5% to its total audience every week as a result of viewers who use a DVR to record the show and then watch it within a week of its initial airing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts for time-shifted viewing when assessing total audience beyond live broadcast figures; indicates the importance of delayed viewing in evaluating a show's real reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewer demographics — income/affluence
rubrics_metrics.description: A March 2007 MAGNA Global report (based on NMR data) showed 30 Rock's viewers have a median income of $65,000, placing the show tied at 11th in affluence among shows; during its second season it ranked fourth among primetime programming for viewers with income above $100,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demographic affluence is used to evaluate the commercial value and advertiser attractiveness of the audience, distinct from raw viewer counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical acclaim and industry awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite struggling ratings, 30 Rock received critical acclaim and multiple awards and nominations (Emmys, Peabody, Writers Guild lists, etc.). The article references award nominations, wins, and critics' lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards and critical recognition are presented as a separate axis of success that may contrast with ratings performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeslot and scheduling effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The article documents many timeslot placements and changes (e.g., Wednesday 8:00 pm EST for first four episodes, multiple Thursday slots across seasons) and notes that the series generally struggled in the ratings despite acclaim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling and timeslot moves are tracked as factors affecting ratings and season performance; specific date ranges and slot shifts are recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syndication/licensing deals and per-episode value
rubrics_metrics.description: Off-network syndication rights for 30 Rock were acquired by Comedy Central and WGN America for about $800,000 an episode (reported in 2009).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary syndication figures indicate downstream commercial value and are used to evaluate a show's financial success beyond initial broadcast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home media release details and extras
rubrics_metrics.description: Universal Studios Home Entertainment released all seven seasons on DVD, with region-specific release dates and extras listed per season (episode commentaries, outtakes, deleted scenes, table reads, behind-the-scenes features, animated webisodes, series finale retrospective, etc.). Complete Collection release also noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Home media contents and release strategy are cataloged as part of the show's distribution and fan-facing value (special features, region differences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Streaming and digital availability / platform moves
rubrics_metrics.description: Episodes available for paid download via Amazon Video, iTunes, Google Play (U.S. only); streaming availability moved between Netflix, Hulu, and Peacock at different times (e.g., moved from Netflix to Hulu on October 1, 2017; returned to Netflix Aug 1, 2021, removed July 31, 2022, moved to Peacock while remaining on Hulu).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streaming platform licensing history is tracked to show where audiences could access the series over time and the shifting rights landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content sensitivity / removal from circulation
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of Fey and co-showrunner Robert Carlock, four episodes that depict actors in blackface were removed from streaming services and taken off circulation on TV in June 2020; Tina Fey apologized, stating that 'intent' is not a free pass and acknowledging the pain caused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal of episodes for racial sensitivity is documented as a post-broadcast content decision affecting availability and public reception; the specific episodes and seasons removed are named.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special programming (live episodes, reunion special) and promotional tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: The series aired special episodes (e.g., a live episode) and in 2020 NBC produced an hour-long reunion special aired without commercials but featuring promotions and tie-ins for NBCUniversal properties; some affiliates declined to air it due to its promotional nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special events and promotional tie-ins are recorded as programming/marketing strategies that can affect distribution, partner relations, and public perception.
